open_decisions.question: BR-044 (low confidence, SME flag): DB2CMT adds 1 to a commit counter on each successful commit, to a rollback counter on each successful rollback and on each successful savepoint restore, and to a savepoint counter on each successful savepoint; the counters accumulate across calls, are reset by 'INIT' and displayed by 'STAT'. Are these statistics a business requirement (and should restores count as rollbacks), or operational output that can be replaced by platform metrics?

Copybook SQLCA (src/copybook/db2/SQLCA.cpy) includes itself (EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA at line 6) and defines only SQL-STATUS-CODES, with no SQLCODE or SQLERRMC field; SQLCODE/SQLERRMC therefore have no Field ID in 14 DB2 programs, including HISTLD00, RTNANA00, RTNCDE00, DB2CMT and DB2CONN. Which SQLCA does the precompiler actually supply, and may the forward design assume the standard DB2 SQLCODE meaning (0 success, -803 duplicate key, negative values errors) used in these requirements?

Copybook SQLCA (FIL-0017) includes itself ('EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA' at line 6) and defines only SQL-STATUS-CODES, with no SQLCODE or SQLERRMC field; SQLCODE/SQLERRMC therefore have no Field ID in the 14 DB2 programs. Which SQLCA layout does the precompiler supply, and may the modern design assume the standard DB2 SQLCODE/SQLERRMC meaning (assumption ASM-004)?

DB2ERR (line 75) uses the non-standard 'ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP'; the ERRPROC logic file flags the same construct (line 57) and PORTDEL uses it for the deletion audit timestamp (source line 169). Which compiler extension is in use and what timestamp format do ERRLOG rows, error-log records and deletion audit records actually carry?

Fifteen elementary level-01 items (e.g. HISTLD00 WS-COMMIT-THRESHOLD, the REPORT-RECORD print lines, DB2CONN WS-CONNECTION-STATE/WS-RETRY-COUNT/WS-MAX-RETRIES, DB2CMT WS-SAVEPOINT-ID) are catalogued as record-level items without Field IDs, so no Java type could be assigned. Should the reverse harness register Field IDs for them, or may later stages map them at record level using the catalogued PIC?

Copybook SQLCA (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0017) line 6 contains 'EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC', naming itself. The included SQL communication area (SQLCODE, SQLSTATE, SQLERRMC, ...) has no layout in any reverse artifact. How should the forward design obtain the SQLCA layout and the SQLCODE/SQLSTATE semantics used by the 14 DB2 programs?

DBPROC procedure code (DB2-ERROR-ROUTINE, lines 47-56) moves data to ERR-PROGRAM and ERR-TEXT and calls 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE, but DBPROC declares none of these and ERR-TEXT is declared in no packet copybook. Which record declares ERR-TEXT / ERR-MESSAGE in each including program, and what is the ERRPROC parameter layout?

Which TRUNC compiler option (STD, OPT or BIN) was used for programs including these copybooks? It decides whether S9(4)/S9(8)/S9(9) COMP fields are truncated to their PIC digits or to the binary halfword/fullword range on store.

The project SQLCA copybook (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0017) includes itself and declares only SQL-STATUS-CODES, while eight packet programs test SQLCODE (and DB2ONLN SQLERRMC), which only the DB2 precompiler's SQLCA supplies. Should the Java design treat SQL status as coming from the SQL driver (SQLException/SQLState) and ignore the project SQLCA content, or must the 35-byte WS-DB2-AREA content be reproduced?

Five record-level 01 elementary items (DB2ERR WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP, WS-FORMATTED-SQLCODE; DB2STAT WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP, WS-START-TIMESTAMP, WS-FORMATTED-TIME) have no Field ID in the reverse catalogue. Should the reverse pipeline register Field IDs for them so they can receive Java types, or may they be modelled by Record ID only?

ERRPROC's LINKAGE LS-ERROR-REQUEST is 354 bytes, but DB2ERR (line 199) and DB2STAT (line 227) CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE from copybook ERRHAND (about 370 bytes, different field order). Which layout is the contract of the Java error service?

Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.
